source.title: A circuit for Python docstrings in a 4-layer attention-only transformer

record.tranche_reason: It investigates induction-head behavior in a new task using attention-pattern analysis and activation patching, rather than reproducing the original training-dynamics measurements.
record.gate_note: The post explicitly identifies head 1.4 as an induction head in the docstring task and reports its attention pattern and patching results. The task can also be solved by other algorithms, so the authors add arguments to isolate the induction-based algorithm. The post mentions initial success finding similar circuits in similarly sized 3- and 4-layer models with MLPs, but does not say specifically that those circuits contain induction-behavior heads or give results for them; V4 is therefore not counted as tested. Training onset, training-loss bumps, large-model in-context learning, and few-shot task learning are not measured.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (Python docstrings, pre-trained attn-only-4l), the authors find head 1.4 acting as an induction head, attending param_3 to B_doc. Patching shows its output carries B_doc information. It relies on a previous-token head (0.2, less certain). This bears on V1's mechanism. Training dynamics, large models, few-shot learning and other families are not measured.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors report a docstring circuit with 3 levels of composition: a def subcircuit (fuzzy previous-token heads 1.4, 2.0), a doc subcircuit (previous-token head 0.2 plus induction head 1.4), and argument mover heads 3.0/3.6. They also report multi-function head 1.4 and head 0.4 deriving position from the causal mask. The circuit recovers up to about half of performance (42% vs 56%), and rigorous composition tests are left for future work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses activation patching and attention-pattern analysis on a pre-trained model and a custom docstring task; does not measure induction-head formation during training or loss-by-token in-context learning.
record.method_sensitivity: Head 1.4's behavior depends on prompt context: it shows induction-like attention for param or an equivalent newline token, fuzzy previous-token behavior for a comma, and is described as inactive for many other tokens. The post also reports that corrupt-token choice can matter. Swapping positional embeddings barely affects head 1.4's attention, while swapping head 0.4's attention pattern inverts its preference.

fits_no_version.finding: Head 1.4's preference for the most recent induction target (B_doc over A_doc) is driven by head 0.4's causal-mask-derived attention pattern. Swapping positional embeddings barely changes it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Induction heads can use causal-mask-derived positional signals from earlier heads to pick the most recent induction target.

fits_no_version.finding: A single head (1.4) acts as an induction head or a fuzzy previous-token head depending on destination token and wider context.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Individual heads can implement induction conditionally, multiplexing with other functions by context.

record.problems: The main analysis uses one model and batches of 50 prompts, with no uncertainty estimates reported. The proposed previous-token head 0.2 is identified with lower confidence. The selected circuit does not recover all model performance, and the post says a more rigorous composition test such as causal scrubbing remains future work.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for the unmodified task's approximately 75% performance or Google-style docstrings: these do not isolate the induction-based algorithm in the reported analysis. No rows for head 0.5's identity-attention result or head 1.2's logit-difference effects, which are auxiliary mechanisms rather than results directly measuring the induction behavior in the claim versions. The mentioned initial success in similar 3- and 4-layer models with MLPs lacks specific induction-head results.

untested.parts: Only one model and one task are examined. There is no test that the mechanism generalizes across small attention-only transformers, and no quantitative composition test (causal scrubbing is left to future work).
There is no training-time formation, abruptness, in-context-learning gain or loss bump.
There are no large models and no loss-by-token measure.
Only 'initial success' is mentioned for similar circuits in 3- and 4-layer MLP models, with no induction-head results.
Training data and setup are not varied. Neel Nanda's comment speculating on data or capacity is not tested.
Few-shot task learning is not studied.

missing.what: Head 1.4 attention on |BOS|S0|A|B|C|S1| prompts by special token. 'param' and newline give an induction-like pattern, ',' gives fuzzy previous-token, and most words attend only to BOS (inactive).
Head 1.4 attends from ,_B to B_def (previous-token role) in the def subcircuit. Random_def patching shows it writes B_def information into ,_B.
missing.locator: Tracking the Flow of the other definition tokens: Attention Head patching

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed to T3 because this is a new task setting on a pre-trained model rather than a method aimed at the original question. Circuit-recovery rows R5–R9 and the performance row R1 do not measure the induction mechanism and were unlinked from V1, which removes the reader's limits_scope label based on them. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Tests a specific docstring-task circuit in one 4-layer attention-only model; the proposed previous-token head is identified with less confidence. Does not establish that this mechanism is general across small attention-only transformers.
No training-time formation, abruptness, in-context-learning gain, or training-loss curve is measured.
No large transformers or general loss-by-token in-context-learning measure.

The post mentions initial success finding similar circuits in 3- and 4-layer models with MLPs, but does not establish that these circuits have induction behavior; no across-family, size, run, architecture, or modality results are reported.
Does not vary training data or setup to test formation or persistence.
Does not study few-shot task learning or compare induction heads with other few-shot mechanisms.
Does not study training transitions or whether formation consists of multiple transitions.

relationships.condition: Head 1.4's induction behaviour across destination tokens and contexts
relationships.reason: From the text, not the rows: head 1.4 shows induction only for param/newline destination tokens and is fuzzy previous-token for commas. It is inactive for most words. Its preference among induction targets comes from head 0.4's causal-mask signal. Head 0.2's role is uncertain (R4).
relationships.display_finding: Head 1.4 showed induction for parameter and newline destinations, fuzzy previous-token attention for commas, and inactivity for most words; head 0.4's causal-mask signal determined preferences among induction targets, while head 0.2's role remained uncertain.
